To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(2),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(2)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(2))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(2).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(2)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(2) & =x \\ f(x) & =2 \\ {x}^{2}-x & =2 \\ {x}^{2}-x-2 & =0 \\ (x+1)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =-1,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of $y=f(x)$ is $x\le -1,$ we have ${f}^{-1}(2)=-1.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(-1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{2}-x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2x-1 \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =2(-1)-1 \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(2) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(2))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-3)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
